Cross-sections of the screens by xOy plane are open smooth Lyapunov type contours. The grating is illuminated by a unit amplitude plane electromagnetic wave. Such structure may serve as one of the models for scatterers system, which has resonance features.

articleTitle: Investigation of solutions of the phase synthesis problem for a circular array
publicationTitle: MMET '96. VIth International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. Proceedings
abstract: The phase synthesis problem according to the prescribed amplitude directivity pattern for a circular array is considered. The variational statement of the problem is used. As an optimization criterion, both the mean-square deviation of the created amplitude directivity pattern from the prescribed one and their weighted inner product are used. The problem is non-linear, and it is solved by successive approximation methods.

articleTitle: Statistical analysis of apodized array pattern characteristics under spatially correlated error influence
publicationTitle: MMET '96. VIth International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. Proceedings
abstract: It is shown that the array pattern parameters under the influence of spatially correlated errors and distortions can and should be optimized in a statistical sense. The proposed sum-type apodization functions (step-like functions also belong to this class) are able to provide the available trade-off of disturbed pattern characteristics. In particular, the mean maximal side lobe level (MSLL) can be reduced by 1.2 dB even in comparison with the optimal Dolph-Chebyshev and Kaiser-Bessel patterns if the initial MSLL is equal. Heuristic recommendations concerning the apodization function selection for a priori known error correlation characteristics and variance are presented.

articleTitle: The resonance on small non-homogeneity in the waveguide
publicationTitle: MMET '96. VIth International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. Proceedings
abstract: The solution of the initial-boundary value problem for the wave equation depending on the small parameter /spl epsiv/, with the right-hand side which is periodic in time with frequency /spl omega/, is researched.

articleTitle: Delaying of transverse surface waves in the isotropic plasma waveguide with the noncircular cross-section
publicationTitle: MMET '96. VIth International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. Proceedings
abstract: Multicomponent waveguide structures with delaying elements are widely used while projecting the radiotechnical devices in plasma and semiconductor electronics. This report is devoted to studying the dispersion properties of the electromagnetic surface waves (SW) of extraordinary polarization with components which propagate across the axis of cylindrical metallic waveguide with plasma insertion.

articleTitle: Construction and application of orthogonal polynomials in kinetics of quasi-particles
publicationTitle: MMET '96. VIth International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. Proceedings
abstract: To determine macroscopic hydrodynamic quantities and kinetic coefficients in different media on the basis of the kinetic theory of particles (quasiparticles), one must know the solution of the kinetic equation for the distribution function. In the kinetic theory of monatomic gases, a set of polynomials is presented by the classical Sonin-Laguerre polynomials. Here, we apply a similar method of calculating kinetic coefficients in a gas of quasiparticles, the energy of which may depend on different external parameters (electrical or magnetic fields, for instance). In this case, the use of classical polynomials appears not to be efficient. Therefore, it is advantageous to construct a special set of orthogonal polynomials on the basis of the weight function characteristic of Bose-Einstein or Fermi-Dirac statistics, a proper choice of which allows us to restrict ourselves to a finite number of first polynomials when calculating kinetic coefficients.

articleTitle: The calculation and optimization of directional characteristics of vibrator antenna with limited dimensional screen
publicationTitle: MMET '96. VIth International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. Proceedings
abstract: Using the uniform geometrical theory of diffraction, algorithms and programs have been derived for calculating and analyzing the directive characteristics of a radiating elementary electric vibrator with an ideally conducting rectangular plane screen at any observation direction. The directive gains of the analyzed system in a normal direction to the screen have been investigated when changing sizes of the screen over wide ranges, for various distances between the vibrator and the screen.

articleTitle: Nonlinear surface magnetic polaritons in non-uniform magnetic field
publicationTitle: MMET '96. VIth International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. Proceedings
abstract: Surface magnetic microwave polaritons of finite amplitude propagating along the interface between ferrite and nonlinear dielectric, located in external weakly non-uniform wall-like magnetic field, are theoretically investigated. The analysis is based on application of variational method added with bilinear relation like Lorenz lemma. It was shown that the wave dispersion and transverse wave profile along field non-uniformity essentially depend on wave amplitude.

articleTitle: Mathematical questions of the boundary equation method in non-stationary problems of the diffraction of electromagnetic waves
publicationTitle: MMET '96. VIth International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. Proceedings
abstract: We develop another approach to the construction of surface retarded potentials. We use directly the fundamental solution /spl Phi/(X) (6/spl times/6 matrix) for the Maxwell system which satisfies the causality condition /spl Phi/(X)=O when t<O. The analog of the third Green formula shows the view of these potentials to us.

articleTitle: Gratings composed of helically conducting cylinders
publicationTitle: MMET '96. VIth International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. Proceedings
abstract: The problem is the diffraction by a grating composed of helically conducting cylinders of radius b with twirl angle /spl Psi/, irradiated by an arbitrarily polarized normally incident plane electromagnetic wave. The helical curves are taken to be right-handed. The grating spacing p is assumed to be less than the wavelength /spl lambda/. That ensures the absence of lateral spectra. Two classes of gratings are considered: with perfect electric and magnetic conductivity of the cylinders simultaneously, and with the electric conductivity only.

articleTitle: Probabilistic analysis of electromagnetic phenomena with stochastic periodicity
publicationTitle: MMET '96. VIth International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. Proceedings
abstract: Both rough recurrence and stochasticity are characteristic features of time changeability of many electromagnetic phenomena. Investigations of stochastic oscillations on the basis of nonstationary random processes of certain classes-periodically correlated, bi-, poly-, and almost periodically correlated-contribute to a wider understanding of oscillation physics. The authors study the probabilistic structure of stochastic recurrence phenomena on the basis of periodically correlated random processes. They develop the methodology and discuss application to the investigation of the probabilistic structure of physical processes.

articleTitle: Spectral approach to filter synthesis in waveguide and quasi optical structures
publicationTitle: MMET '96. VIth International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. Proceedings
abstract: The traditional problems of filtering acquire, in the millimeter (mm) wave range, a number of peculiarities, consisting first of all in increasing requirements on the accuracy of design and manufacturing components. This work describes the spectral synthesis, strong analysis and theoretical investigation of band-pass (BPF) and band-stop filters (BSF) in waveguides and periodic grating angular (BPFA) or frequency (BPFF) band-pass filters in quasi optical structures. All synthesis and analysis algorithms are based on rigorous mathematical models.

articleTitle: Mathematical model of losses in multi-mode optical fibers at guide axis bends
publicationTitle: MMET '96. VIth International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. Proceedings
abstract: The peculiarity of optical-fiber data transmission systems is that it is necessary to lay fibers into optical modules with comparative reserve to eliminate fiber strain effects. It is necessary to find the parameters of fiber bend in an optical module with given fiber-loss level, construction length interval, comparative cable lengthening and primary fiber characteristics. To solve this problem it is necessary to obtain the analytical dependence of whole mode stream losses vs. bend parameters and primary optical-fiber characteristics. The analysis of mode (or mode-group) energy interchange within the bend leads to the energy diffusion equation.

articleTitle: Computation of the eigenmodes' system of generalized slotline by means of the domains' product technique
publicationTitle: MMET '96. VIth International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. Proceedings
abstract: Presents an approach to the numerical analysis of a generalized slotline having a polygonal cross-section form. The solution of the eigenmodes problem is based on the domains' product technique. The distinguishing characteristic of the algorithm is the possibility of substantial variation of the structures geometry within the framework of the chosen mathematical model. Numerical computations of dispersion characteristics for particular cases of the above transmission line are presented. The validity of the approach has been confirmed by comparing the obtained results with the data of other authors.

articleTitle: Numerical technique of non stationary electromagnetic theory
publicationTitle: MMET '96. VIth International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. Proceedings
abstract: Initial boundary value problems (ibvp) and boundary value problems (bvp) for Maxwell's system of differential equations are the subjects under investigation in electromagnetic theory. That is the starting mathematical model of physical processes, and it is necessary by means of mathematical techniques to extract and treat the physical results. The main subject of the present communication is the review of modern methods and algorithms for numerical analyses of transient processes in open compact, waveguide and periodic resonators. Computation of scattering characteristics of elementary discontinuities is of special importance. We have developed specialized algorithms, using formally correct numerical subroutines in key steps of solution construction, including analytical regularization of operator equations of the first kind.

articleTitle: Propagation of ultra-short optical pulses in nonlinear optical fibers: an analysis by the beam propagation method
publicationTitle: MMET '96. VIth International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. Proceedings
abstract: The beam propagation method has been applied to determine the behavior of ultra-short optical pulses in lossless and lossy guides. The method can be applied for arbitrary shapes of initial pulses. The computations were carried out for rectangular pulses and a pair of solitons.

articleTitle: Joint use of generalized scattering matrices and domains' product technique in theory of complicated planar waveguide structures
publicationTitle: MMET '96. VIth International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. Proceedings
abstract: A technique of utilization of generalized scattering matrices (S-matrices) for numerical analysis of H-and E-plane waveguide transforms having polygonal boundaries and piece-wise homogeneous filler is developed. The method of decomposition of such objects, providing the possibility of calculating S-matrices of isolated autonomous blocks by means of the domains' product (DP) method, has been proposed. Some illustrative examples are considered.

articleTitle: Subsurface layer statistical resonance
publicationTitle: MMET '96. VIth International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. Proceedings
abstract: When considering the scattering of waves by a layered medium with a rough surface, the correlator Q=<E(/spl omega/)E(/spl omega/)> is usually studied (here E and /spl omega/ are the electric field of the reflected wave and the circular frequency, correspondingly). Generally, it can be expanded in a power series of the reflection coefficients V/sub i/ of inner boundaries. For the case of strong scattering the terms Q/sub i1/ proportional to the first powers of V/sub i/ become as a rule exponentially small by the scattering parameter /spl Delta/=(/spl sigma///spl lambda/)/sup 2/, with /spl sigma/ and /spl lambda/ being the mean square roughness height and the wave length accordingly. Only if more general correlators P are considered, then the values P/sub i1/ prove to be not exponentially small when some resonance conditions are satisfied. We refer to this phenomena as to the subsurface layer statistical resonance. For the first time, we found that the phenomena exist in the two cases: of small jump of the dielectric constant at the medium boundary and of large-scale roughness for normal incidence of wave. In this report we generalise the last case for oblique incidence of wave. It is shown, that the resonance takes place in a specular direction for the two frequency correlator P=<E(/spl omega//sub 1/)E(/spl omega//sub 2/)> with the resonance condition /spl omega//sub 1,2/=/spl omega//sub 2,1/(/spl radic/(/spl epsiv/-sin/sup 2//spl theta/)/cos/spl theta/-1). Here /spl epsiv/ and /spl theta/ are the layer dielectric constant and the incident angle, accordingly. The resonance width and amplitude are studied and discussed.

articleTitle: Ray tracing fields in a dichroic radome enclosing a Hertzian dipole
publicationTitle: MMET '96. VIth International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. Proceedings
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to present some results from an on-going study of curved frequency selective surfaces (FSS). Here we consider an FSS consisting of an array of ring slots in a conducting sheet, centrally embedded in a dielectric.

articleTitle: Mathematical models of diffraction and radiation problems for planar waveguide with impedance flange
publicationTitle: MMET '96. VIth International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. Proceedings
abstract: The problem of diffraction and radiation for a planar semibounded waveguide with ideally conducting sides and flange has been solved by different methods more than once. In this work the problem is considered in the impedance flange case. The derivation of a singular integral equation is demonstrated in the radiation problem case.

articleTitle: Weak radiation condition in the problem of a plane wave diffraction by a wedge
publicationTitle: MMET '96. VIth International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. Proceedings
abstract: The Kontorovich-Lebedev transform is used for the solution of various problems of diffraction by a wedge. A failure of this transform is that it is applicable to a narrow class of functions not containing, in particular, a complete solution to the problem of diffraction. To overcome this problem a modified Kontorovich-Lebedev transform has previously been obtained in which the two-dimensional equation is reduced to an ordinary differential equation. The authors obtain a generalized radiation condition to give sense to this equation for the problem of plane wave diffraction by a wedge.

articleTitle: Diffraction by the dielectric disk and by the circular dielectric window in the perfectly conducting screen
publicationTitle: MMET '96. VIth International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. Proceedings
abstract: The geometrical theory of diffraction (GTD) can be applied to dielectric structures with a surface wave, but it is necessary to solve new canonical problems and to generalize the definition of the diffraction coefficient. As an example of the new canonical problem, we consider electromagnetic wave scattering by an edge of the semi-infinite dielectric slab. It is appropriate to describe the interdependence between amplitudes of the incident waves and scattering or reflecting waves (space and surface) in matrix form. Our task is to find the radar cross-section of the dielectric disk.

articleTitle: Remote sensing of water salinity
publicationTitle: MMET '96. VIth International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. Proceedings
abstract: For the remote sensing of water surface salinity we use the radar method of measuring the power reflection coefficient which is defined by the complex dielectric constant (CDC). The same parameter, in fact, is estimated in UHF radiometric measurements of water salinity. In the case considered here of normal incidence of a plane electromagnetic wave on a smooth water surface the value of the reflection coefficient is defined by the Fresnel relation.

articleTitle: On the diffraction of electromagnetic waves by biconical structure with longitudinal slots
publicationTitle: MMET '96. VIth International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. Proceedings
abstract: The three-dimensional rigorous boundary-value problem of electromagnetic wave scattering by a perfectly conducting biconical structure with longitudinal slots is considered. The effect of longitudinal slots on scattering characteristics is investigated. It is well known that singularities of the boundary (vertices, edges, slots, etc.) affect scattering characteristics. The investigation of field behavior in the vicinity of singular points represents a special interest. The analytical solution of these boundary-value problems makes it possible to study, in particular, distinctive features of screens and field behavior near boundary singularities. The biconical structure under consideration consists of two coaxial circular semi-infinite perfectly conducting cones with periodic slots cut along generatrices. There are some interesting particular cases of this structure such as a plane angular sector, a cone with longitudinal slots, and a biconical surface consisting of the cone with longitudinal slots and an isotropic one.

articleTitle: Diffraction on compound boundary structures
publicationTitle: MMET '96. VIth International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. Proceedings
abstract: Deals with the problem of diffraction of a plane electromagnetic E-polarized simple harmonic wave falling on a compound boundary structure at an angle /spl alpha/. Maxwell equations that describe the model can be reduced to the Helmholtz equation.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic waves transmission through grounded waveguide with scatterers
publicationTitle: MMET '96. VIth International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. Proceedings
abstract: Investigation of the properties of fields, diffracted on a system of scatterers in a stratified medium, is an important problem of modern radiophysics. Description of such phenomena in the resonance frequency range, where the wavelength is close to the scatterers' dimensions, is possible only with a rigorous solution of the corresponding diffraction problem. Significant difficulties arise when the scattered field is calculated in the case of arbitrary scatterer geometry. One way to solve the problem of scalar electromagnetic wave diffraction in the H-polarized case on scatterers in a stratified medium is proposed.

articleTitle: Eigen electromagnetics wave in round waveguide with biisotropic mode
publicationTitle: MMET '96. VIth International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. Proceedings
abstract: The general method for determination of the structure of fields and integrated characteristics consists of construction of Maxwell equations for a boundless biisotropic environment on the basis of which, in view of the boundary conditions, is formed an eigenvalue equation. We describe an alternative approach consisting of the numerical integration of a system of wave equations with given boundary conditions. This permits us to expand the class of soluble problems and to consider waveguides of continually non-uniform structure with biisotropic cross section by filling.

articleTitle: The Kontorovich-Lebedev transform in diffraction problems for conical surfaces
publicationTitle: MMET '96. VIth International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. Proceedings
abstract: One powerful analytical method for solution of diffraction problems in regions with conical boundaries is the method of the Kontorovich-Lebedev integral transform. The inversion formula is preferable for solution of diffraction problems or for calculation of the far field. In the case of boundary conditions such as the Dirichlet or the Neumann condition for the Helmholz equation, algebraic equations for transforms are established and solutions are found easy by means of the inversion formula. Difficulties begin in problems with boundary conditions of the third kind which depend on radial coordinates. The situation takes place for conic surfaces conducting along spirals, for instance. In this case for transforms we can obtain linear nonhomogeneous fnnctional equations with entire differences and complex coefficients including the associated Legendre functions.

articleTitle: The matrix theory of non uniform waveguide structures excitation
publicationTitle: MMET '96. VIth International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. Proceedings
abstract: The present paper suggests a new matrix-electrodynamics method, which is based on the selection among the direct and backward waves of a more narrow class of waves, marked in correspondence with the location of excitation sources relative to the region being considered. A non-uniform waveguide structure (WS) means any fast or slow change of the form or size of its cross section, parameters of dielectric filling, metal or dielectric ledges, probes, coupling apertures, etc. As an example, the authors consider a waveguide-microstrip junction.

articleTitle: Rigorous theory of rectangular waveguide multiple-slot couplers
publicationTitle: MMET '96. VIth International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. Proceedings
abstract: A new high efficient quasi-analytical field theory method for the analysis of multiple-slot directional couplers is proposed. The theory is based on one of the versions of the Galerkin's method in which the weighted Gegenbauer polynomials are used as the basis functions explicitly taking into account the edge condition. Another important feature of the presented theory is the separation and analytical transform of the matrix operator static part of the obtained linear algebraic equations set. The results are in good agreement with theoretical and experimental data of other work.

articleTitle: The sensitivity of four-coil electromagnetic transducer to electric conductivity anisotropy
publicationTitle: MMET '96. VIth International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. Proceedings
abstract: The problem of interaction of electromagnetic waves with anisotropic conductive media was considered in some earlier works. But it is not possible to use this results for analyzing of the eddy current probe signals. The known theoretical models cannot describe new electromagnetic multi-coil probes especially in the case when the probe is located under anisotropic conductive material. In this paper we present the theoretical investigation of the influence of electric conductivity anisotropy on the output signal of four-coil displaced probe.

articleTitle: Mixed potential integral equation methods for multilayered structures
publicationTitle: MMET '96. VIth International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory. Proceedings
abstract: Electromagnetic fields created in a homogeneous medium by a known distribution of electric current are determined by integral equations involving free space Green's functions. In actual situations, however, current distributions are not known beforehand and must be determined, in such a way that the total fields satisfy the boundary conditions on the conductors. The integral equation technique was extended to treat also heterogeneous structures, in order to analyze and design multilayer printed circuits and antennas, such as the broadband strip-slot-foam-inverted patch printed antenna. Sommerfeld integrals provide Green's functions for stratified media, which are evaluated by means of specifically developed, efficient computer algorithms. Structures including coaxial or line feeds and coupling through slots can now be easily analyzed with commercially available software packages.
